reference: Olkiluoto, Finland, crystalline bedrock (no published log for these boxes), wet

description.lithology: Dark grey to black, medium-grained mafic to intermediate metamorphic rock with a strongly foliated / gneissic fabric. The groundmass is dark, fine to medium grained, with irregular to patchy lighter grey to white leucocratic intervals / lenses. The fabric is strongly foliated with a wavy to mottled appearance; the white material appears as quartz +/- feldspar segregations / lenses within the dark matrix. No definitive primary igneous texture is resolvable at photo resolution; the rock is consistent with an amphibolite / mafic gneiss with intercalated leucocratic material.
description.alteration: none visible. No obvious chloritic, sericitic, silicified, potassic, carbonate or oxidised alteration can be confidently identified in the photo resolution.
description.mineralization: none visible. No visible sulfides or ore minerals such as pyrite, chalcopyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite or galena can be discerned in the image.

anomalies.explanation: Core is broken into multiple pieces along the tray with visible fractures; the top row shows a broken piece at the right end and the second row shows a broken piece at the right end, the fourth row shows a fracture near the right end and the bottom row shows a fracture near the right end.
Wooden depth markers are present at 23.66 m on the second row left, and at 26.70 m and 27.20 m on the bottom row left and right, indicating the run spans approximately 23.66 to 27.20 m.

White to light grey quartz-rich patches / lenses are visible throughout the core, most prominent in the top row and fourth row, consistent with a lithological variation or quartz veining that should be checked in hand specimen.
